newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian prosecutor seeks to indict ex-Nazi officer.
newsitem.headline: Italian prosecutor seeks to indict ex-Nazi officer.

text.p: A Turin military prosecutor said on Wednesday he wanted to put another former Nazi SS officer on trial one day after a military court in Rome handed down a verdict in Italy's most sensational war crimes trial.

Prosecutor Pier Paolo Rivello told Reuters in a telephone interview he had asked a military court to indict 86-year-old Theodor Saewecke, who held the rank of captain, on charges of "violence to Italian citizens through homocide."

He allegedly ordered the murders of 15 Italian civilians, on August 10, 1944, as a reprisal for a partisan bomb attack in which Nazi officers were killed. The bodies of the victims were displayed in a central Milan square.

On Tuesday, a Rome court ordered former SS captain Erich Priebke, 83, to serve five years in jail for his role in Italy's worst World War Two massacre at the Ardeatine Caves in March 1944 in which 335 men and boys were rounded up and shot.
His co-defendent Karl Hass, 84, was set free.

Saewecke, who served as a Nazi police captain in Milan during the German occupation, was now living in Germany, but Rivello said he would not seek his extradition unless he was brought to trial and found guilty.
An indictment hearing should be held mid-October, he said.
"It would be up to him to attend the trial. But I hope he would, so he could lay out his views," Rivello said.

He said he had not questioned Saewecke, but had received a statement in which he defended the shootings, saying both German troops and Italian partisans had carried out killings. "In the statement, Saewecke shows no sign of regret," Rivello said.
